items.title: 68087_Cliff Leeman oral history interview
items.q: The interviewer mentions Bernie Privin as someone they used to work with. The interviewee (Cliff Leeman) does not mention Bernie Privin in their response, nor does he confirm a personal or professional relationship with him.

ctx.x: Pee Wee Irwin -- of course, I first knew him when I was with -- when he was with the Tommy Dorsey Band, and in '39 along with Yank Lawson on trumpets and so forth and so on, and I -- when Bobby Hackett left Nick's that first year, I stayed on and this is 1950 -- I stayed on and Pee Wee Irwin became the leader, and I'd done much work and recordings and concerts with Pee Wee over the years. We've been more than friends. I went to Britain with Pee Wee; Scotland, England, London, Edinburgh, Stockholm, Sweden, Germany…

It was some band; there was Bernie Privin, the guy I used to work with in the old Artie Shaw and Charlie Barnet days, and he had been in the studios for years; he's a wonderful trumpet player in the Louis Armstrong vein. Dick

Hyman was on piano with us and Major Holley on base; Ed Hubbie on trombone, Kenny Davern -- he played both the clarinet and primarily the soprano saxophone -- I have a mental block with that word 'soprano'.
